name: frozen
reason: json_walk(bytes, length, callback) reports typed tokens (string, number, true, false, null, object and array start/end) with paths, so the format is interpreted; but values stay raw spans. Its documented json_unescape decodes the control's \u00e9 to the single byte 0xE9 (probe: 'caf\u00e9 \"quoted\"' -> 636166e9202271756f74656422) instead of UTF-8 C3 A9, and the source returns JSON_STRING_INVALID for any \uXXXX above U+00FF. The nested-object control therefore cannot match the Python oracle; numbers are not converted by the library. Not built into a harness.

name: jsmn
reason: Decided against PROTOCOL.md's eligibility rule for this cell's value gate: jsmn_parse fills token spans typed only as object, array, string or primitive with child counts. It does not distinguish numbers, booleans and null, does not decode string escapes, and builds no values; reproducing the control's nested value would require the harness to interpret JSON itself. The token structure is observable but is not the parsed value the other rows verify. Not built.

name: liblaxjson
reason: lax_json_feed/lax_json_eof with event callbacks rejects the nested-object control at -0.25e1 ('unexpected character': its exponent state requires an explicit '+' or '-' sign, which RFC 8259 makes optional), and every number reaches the only number callback as an atof() double, so integer/float kinds are not observable on either control. Not selected; 1 Debian installation.
